# `⍒` — Grade down / Grade down by

Function. Keys: `Alt-Backslash g`. Ranks: `∞` monadic, `∞ ∞` dyadic

`⍒Y` gives indices that sort major cells descending. Stable, with the same [ordering](delta-stile.qmd) as Grade up.

```bpl
⍒30 10 20          ⍝ [0 2 1]ₓ
⍒2 1 2 1           ⍝ [0 2 1 3]ₓ
```

`C⍒Y` uses character collation `C`.

```bpl
"cba"⍒"abc"        ⍝ [0 1 2]ₓ
```

See [`>`](greater-than.qmd) to sort.

## Fast combinations

These trains and compositions give the result of applying their parts in turn, faster. [Trains](../evaluation.qmd#trains) says which spellings BPL recognises.

| Combination | Applies to | Benefit |
|---|---|---|
| `k↑⍒ Y` or `(k↑)∘⍒` | a vector of reals or characters without keys, with the count at most a quarter of its length | selects the first `k` positions of the descending grade, or the last `-k`, without ordering the rest |
| `↑⍒ Y`, `i⌷⍒ Y` or `i⊃⍒ Y` | the same vectors | selects one position without ordering the rest |
| `⍋⍒ Y` or `⍋∘⍒` | any `Y` without keys on its first axis | gives each major cell's rank in descending order by inverting the grade, without grading it again |

```bpl
v←30 10 20 50 40 60 70 80 90 0
2↑⍒ v                                ⍝ [8 7]ₓ
⍋⍒ v                                 ⍝ [6 8 7 4 5 3 2 1 0 9]ₓ
(•explain "2↑⍒ v").fast.combination  ⍝ ["partial grade"]
```

## Inverse

`⍒⁻¹P` gives an array whose descending grade is the permutation `P`. Any other `P` is a `DOMAIN` error.

```bpl
⍒⁻¹2 0 1   ⍝ [1 0 2]ₓ
```
